Subject: Tenant-level storage & erase capabilities (Meadowview)

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. As Meadowview moves several regulated workloads onto Redwood, our security team has two core asks we need clarified before procurement can progress:

1) Can tenants choose a storage region at account/tenant creation (for data residency)? We need a per-tenant selection that guarantees customer data sticks to a region (US/EU) except for system metadata.

2) For data subject requests and incident response, can we perform an on-demand permanent erase for a single tenant that removes data from live stores and is logged/auditable? Important: we also need guidance on backups/snapshots — will deleted data persist in backups and for how long after an erase?

Attached is our SOC2 evidence request and a short list of questions. Can you loop in engineering or product to explain capabilities and timeline?

Appreciate it,
Lena Ortiz

Thanks for looping me in, Ava. Quick technical summary and recommended defaults: 

Summary of current state (approx):
- Per-tenant region routing: supported at write time via tenant metadata routing. We can provision tenant mappings to a preferred region (us/eu/apac) for primary storage. However, some control-plane metadata remains global.
- On-demand erase: we have a reversible soft-delete pathway today (soft-delete flag + retention window). Permanent irreversible erase (purge from live stores + index removal + KV cache eviction) exists as an engineering script used in emergency ops but is not exposed via a supported API.
- Backups & snapshots: nightly snapshots are retained for 30 days for most clusters and are currently region-local, but some cross-region replication exists for DR in certain deployments. Purging from backups requires a retention-policy change and restore+re-seed process; there is no instant global backup purge.

Risks / caveats:
- For guaranteed regional sovereignty, we must ensure no cross-region replicas are created for that tenant. That requires a configuration guardrail and potentially dedicated tenant placement in region-specific pools for stronger guarantees.
- Permanent erase today is manual and has two risks: (1) it may not remove data from historical snapshots immediately; (2) auditability is limited because the workflow relies on ops-runbooks rather than a first-class audit log entry.

Proposed short-term offer we can safely make to Meadowview (v1):
- Tenant region preference: support setting a "preferred_region" at tenant creation. We'll configure their tenant to US-only primary storage and confirm no cross-region replication is enabled for their deployment. (Ops action + config)
- On-demand erase: Offer a supervised permanent erase service where ops runs a documented purge playbook and provides a signed deletion report (artifact). We'll include a list of affected stores and a timestamped audit note. This is not self-serve yet.

Implementation timeline estimate (if approved):
- Supervised purge workflow + deletion reporting: ~2 weeks to formalize runbook + audit template (ops + security + legal sign-off). Task: INF-2319.
- API + UI to make erase self-serve + audit log entries + backup purge coordination: Q3 roadmap (6-10 weeks) — requires product + infra + backups team.
- Stronger region guarantees (prevent cross-region replica creation at infra/orchestration level): Q3–Q4 roadmap depending on resource allocation.

Questions for product (Marissa):
- Does product want to offer the supervised purge as an official entitled service or treat as a one-off managed service?
- Prioritization: is tenant-level retention & erase self-serve in scope for H2? If yes, I can add spec notes and link to INF-2319.

Priyom
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Core

Great context — thanks Priyom. Summarizing a product recommendation we can communicate to Meadowview and what we'll commit to as a short-term and roadmap plan.

What we can tell Meadowview now (short-term / conservative):
- Placement: We will provision Meadowview into a US-only tenant placement and explicitly disable cross-region replication. We'll document the limitations (control-plane metadata global; backups retained per the retention window).
- Supervised erase: We will offer a documented, ops-executed permanent erase with a signed deletion report and a post-action audit entry. This will be delivered as a managed service (not self-serve) while we build product features.

Proposed roadmap (recommended prioritization):
- Phase 0 (this sprint, 2 weeks): Formalize supervised-erase runbook + audit template (deliverable: deletion report template + ops checklist). Owner: Priyom + Security.
- Phase 1 (Q3): Tenant Config UI/API — allow administrators to set preferred_region and retention_ttl per tenant (soft-delete behavior remains). Deliverables: Admin API, console controls, doc pages. Owner: Product + Platform.
- Phase 2 (Q3–Q4): Self-serve permanent erase with audit logs + retention coordination for backups. Deliverables: irreversible purge API, audit trail entries, backup purge strategy + docs. Owner: Platform + Storage.
- Phase 3 (Q4+): Strong placement guarantees (prevent cross-region replicas for tenants with sovereignty requirement) and optional per-tenant dedicated capacity. Deliverables: orchestration placement changes + SLA updates.

Ask / decision points for Sales/Security:
- Do we want to price supervised erase as a billable managed service or include it as part of enterprise contracts for the next 6 months? (Sales input: Sean)
- Are Meadowview's requirements (as written) sufficient acceptance criteria for the supervised erase report? Lena, can you confirm what evidence your auditor will need?

Next steps:
- Ava: confirm Meadowview POC urgency and whether they want a formal proposal.
- Priyom: create INF-2319 ticket and attach runbook draft (start with the deletion report template we discussed).
- Sean: advise on commercial positioning of the managed erase offering.

I'll draft a concise reply to Meadowview that lays out the short-term offer and the timeline we just agreed on.

— Marissa Cole
Sr Product Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
